  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "For Time-to-Target: Test H0: mu_Combined = mu_ICMS = mu_Dim = mu_Bright = mu_Sham against H1: at least one mean differs.",
    "For Success: Since the variable is binary (0/1), treat as a proportion; use ANOVA on raw scores as an approximation or prefer Chi-square test of homogeneity, but proceed with ANOVA if normality can be approximated via large n.",
    "For Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD: Test H0: all group means are equal against H1: at least one differs.",
    "Set significance level alpha = 0.05 for all omnibus tests."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Verify that each row represents a unique trial from a distinct mouse or that trials are independent within mice (check for repeated measures structure in raw data if available; current summary suggests pooled data).",
    "Normality of residuals: Check Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals of each ANOVA model. Note: 'Success' is binary and likely violates normality; 'Path Efficiency' has a highly skewed distribution (min 0.0009, max 29.8, mean 0.47, sd 0.46), suggesting a non-normal distribution that may require transformation (e.g., log or square root) or non-parametric alternatives.",
    "Homogeneity of variances: Check Levene's test or Bartlett's test across the five paradigm groups for each response variable.",
    "Outliers: Inspect boxplots for extreme values, particularly in 'Time-to-Target' (max 201.39 vs mean 2.80) and 'Path Efficiency' (max 29.8 vs mean 0.47), which could unduly influence results.",
    "For 'Success': Given the binary nature and large sample size (n=76655), the Central Limit Theorem may allow ANOVA, but a Chi-square test of independence or logistic regression is statistically more appropriate."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any omnibus ANOVA F-test yields p < 0.05, proceed with post-hoc pairwise comparisons.",
    "Use Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test for all pairwise comparisons to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "For 'Success', if ANOVA is deemed inappropriate, use pairwise Chi-square tests with Bonferroni correction, or post-hoc contrasts from a logistic regression model.",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared for ANOVA, Cohen's h for proportions) for significant differences.",
    "Generate interaction plots (if treating Mouse as a blocking factor in a mixed model) or group means plots with 95% confidence intervals to visualize differences."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Significant differences are expected in 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' given the large disparity in means and ranges across paradigms (e.g., Combined likely outperforming Sham).",
    "'Success' rates may vary significantly, with 'Combined' potentially showing higher success than 'Sham' or single-modality conditions.",
    "'Average Speed' and 'AD' (angular dispersion) are expected to show significant differences, with 'Combined' likely exhibiting higher speed and lower AD (better precision) compared to control conditions.",
    "The 'Dim Visual Only' and 'Bright Visual Only' conditions may show intermediate performance compared to 'ICMS Only' and 'Sham', depending on the specific navigation task demands."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset summary does not indicate whether 'Mouse' is treated as a random effect; if multiple trials per mouse exist, a standard one-way ANOVA violates independence assumptions, and a repeated-measures ANOVA or linear mixed-effects model is required.",
    "Highly skewed distributions for 'Path Efficiency' and extreme outliers in 'Time-to-Target' may violate ANOVA assumptions, necessitating data transformation or non-parametric tests (e.g., Kruskal-Wallis).",
    "The binary nature of 'Success' makes ANOVA less ideal than categorical analysis methods.",
    "No information on sample size per group is provided in the summary, though the total N is large; imbalance in group sizes (e.g., Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) could affect power and assumption validity."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a linear mixed-effects model for each response variable with 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures, followed by likelihood ratio tests and post-hoc pairwise comparisons with Tukey adjustment."
}
